A1.justification: Both PDFs describe rePIRL. All 18 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison. Added sections and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original math and coding evaluations in Table 2, application experiments in Figure 1, and design ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds stochastic-decoding evaluations, training curves and policy-entropy measurements.

M1.justification: The learning objectives and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. V2 documents an equivalent log-space/Softmax implementation of importance weighting; its explanation of average process rewards describes a calculation already present in v1's Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: The five math and two coding benchmarks, Eurus training data, and MATH-based application scenarios are retained. The added evaluations reuse existing math coverage without introducing new tasks or domains.

E2.justification: V2 newly evaluates Intuitor against rePIRL and RLOO in the Section 5 entropy comparison. The seven main baselines remain unchanged; the added stochastic and learning-curve comparisons otherwise use previously evaluated methods.

E3.justification: New Appendix C evaluates expected pass@1 at temperature 0.6 with 16 responses per prompt. Appendix E adds learning-curve evaluation on MATH-500. The main greedy-decoding protocol, two-epoch training budget and Eurus-based checkpoint selection remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds focused checks of decoding sensitivity, convergence and training stability, and entropy collapse. Existing expert-source, reward-model-size, RL-algorithm, importance-sampling and rollout-strategy ablations are retained, moving from Appendix C to Appendix D.

E5.justification: V2 introduces sampling-based estimation of expected pass@1 by averaging 16 independent responses per prompt. This documents response sampling, without establishing additional training runs. Training-seed variability, confidence intervals and significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results and Figures 1–3 are unchanged. New Table 4 reports stochastic math averages of 30.8 versus RLOO's 30.1 for 3B, and 38.5 versus PRIME's 37.5 for 4B. These are additional settings, not improvements over v1 scores. V2 also adds learning curves, entropy values of 0.11/0.12/0.028 for rePIRL/RLOO/Intuitor, and RLOO's nine-hour training time.

T1.justification: The theorem, four propositions, assumptions and Appendix A proofs retain their mathematical substance. The added log-weight expression is equivalent to existing importance weights; minor prose edits do not change the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about minimally constrained IRL-based PRM learning, unification of prior methods, reasoning performance and PRM applications. The additions support existing claims without redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: V2 expands the efficiency discussion from comparison with PRIME to acknowledging overhead relative to RLOO and arguing that PRM reuse justifies it. It also interprets the new entropy and learning-curve evidence as supporting avoidance of over-determinism and stable optimization.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, documents log-space importance weights with minibatch Softmax, and explains the existing average-reward calculation. It supplies settings for the added analyses and RLOO timing. The original hyperparameter table and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chen et al. (2021), Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code, in connection with non-greedy pass@1 evaluation. The related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain unchanged; the revised Hu reference describes the same work.

P1.justification: V2 adds localized explanations and discussion, introduces Appendices C and E, and renames the existing ablation appendix D. It updates contribution/affiliation/publication information, adds acknowledgements and corrects a cross-reference. Most prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds stochastic-results Table 4 and training-curves Figure 4. Existing Tables 4–6 become Tables 5–7, with some relocation and two row-header corrections from Dataset to Model. Existing figures are retained, alongside limited first-page and appendix layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for the retained method through stochastic-decoding validation and direct stability/entropy diagnostics. Implementation explanations and the code link improve reproducibility information. These are useful, bounded gains; the principal evaluation and theory remain unchanged, and the new stability analyses do not establish variability across training runs.
